title: Phase Shift and Sinusoidal Transformations
originalTopic: General Sinusoids: Factoring the Phase Shift
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the amplitude, period, and horizontal phase shift of the cosine function y = 3*cos(2x - pi/3).

steps.title: Factor the Argument into Standard Form
steps.explanation: To identify the true horizontal phase shift, factor out the frequency coefficient B = 2 from the entire argument expression.
steps.why: The standard transformation formula y = A*cos(B(x - C)) requires a unit coefficient on x inside the inner factor.

steps.title: Identify Amplitude and Period
steps.explanation: The amplitude is |A| = 3. The period is 2*pi divided by B = 2, which equals pi.
steps.why: Periodic horizontal scaling compresses the cycle by factor 1/B.

steps.title: State the Phase Shift
steps.explanation: Because the expression inside the factored parentheses is (x - pi/6), the wave is shifted horizontally to the right by pi/6 units.
steps.why: Subtracting a positive constant C from x translates the waveform rightward.
